pairs.difference: A is the cooler card from the real anchor sheet: a flat sea horizon, a few cloud puffs, plain sand and ice/cans inside the container. B is a paddling pool in a fenced yard. It has a fence corner across the top and grass covered in scattered small blade tufts, plus a duck in the water. The pool and fence are a reasonable category-4 setting. The repeated grass tufts add small detail that the real cards do not have.
pairs.fix: Paddling pool on a smooth, even lawn with no separate grass tufts or blades. Keep only the wooden fence, plain and softly lit, cut by the top edge of the card. Keep the one rubber duck floating in the water.

pairs.difference: Both are flat objects lying on a wood surface that fills the card, seen from above. A's envelope sits on planks with darker grain seams. B's book sits on streaky lighter wood with a warm glow and a heavy drop shadow. The stickers on B's cover belong to the object, so they are outside my vector. On staging alone, nothing separates the two.
Both umbrellas float on the same quiet tone-on-tone concentric ring field, with no props or decoration. The staging is the same.
A's gloves lie on a pink wave pattern. B's fan floats on a yellow wave pattern with a brighter glow at the centre. Both backdrops are quiet and tone-on-tone, and neither card adds props.

Both chairs stand on a glossy wood floor in front of a vertical-stripe wall. A's room is cyan with a diagonal floor line. B's is blue with a soft light behind the chair. Both are category 3 with nothing added.
The jacket floats on a green sunburst and the hat on a blue sunburst. Both are plain category-1 cards with no props.

A's inkwell stands on a plain wooden desk in front of a yellow striped wall. That is a quiet category-3 setup, and the quill is a partner object in use. B puts a fountain on a round plaza of many small paving tiles that wraps to the card edges, but behind it is the same flat striped wall. That mixes an outdoor place with a graphic backdrop, and the tiles add a lot of small edges (edge density 0.046, top of the real range).
pairs.fix: Stone fountain standing on a plain, smooth stone floor in the same warm colour as the backdrop, with no paving tiles. Behind it, a simple yellow wall with soft wide stripes.

pairs.difference: B's gramophone stands on a glossy wood table in front of a deep purple sunburst. That is quiet, like the real anchor cards. A's wheel stands on a curved cartoon deck whose planks have drawn lines and crack marks, in front of a washed-out pastel pink/lilac sunburst. The floor lines add busy, sketchy detail, and the pale backdrop does not match the game's saturated fields.
pairs.fix: Ship's wheel on its stand on a smooth, polished wooden deck with no drawn cracks or grain lines. Behind it, a saturated sunburst in a single colour.

pairs.difference: A hangs the stage light from a steel truss lattice that runs across the whole top edge, with coloured light beams crossing the backdrop. The background is full of small, high-contrast cross-bracing (edge density 0.061, far above the real 0.004–0.017). B's coral stands on a plain green floor in front of a quiet green wave field. Its few rocks are part of the coral base.
pairs.fix: Stage spotlight hanging from one simple dark bar at the top of the card, with no lattice truss. The backdrop is a soft teal-blue gradient with one faint wide light beam.

pairs.difference: The ring box is on a blue sunburst and the pocket watch on a quiet green diamond pattern. Both float on graphic fields with nothing invented around them.

A shows the whole door from a distance. It is surrounded by a full brick wall, bougainvillea in two corners, two flower bushes, stone steps, a paved path, dappled leaf shadows and scattered pink petals. That is many objects and a lot of small detail (edge density 0.244, about three times the real maximum). B is close in on the wreath where it hangs on the door. The door and ivy frame are cut by the card edges, which is the real category-4 crop, although the ivy leaves are still busy.
pairs.fix: Close view of the door filling the card, cut by the card edges. Around it, a plain smooth wall with one or two large, soft leaf shapes at most. No flower bushes, steps, paving or fallen petals.

pairs.difference: Both stand on a plain purple seamless floor in the backdrop's colour, with a soft glow (category 2). The cans on the vending-machine shelves are its contents, and the teacup's steam belongs to the object.

pattern: The lessons all point the same way: generated cards build more environment than the real ones. They pull back to show the whole object, and they add invented props (rocks, lifebuoys, plant clumps) and sprinkled small details (petals, grass tufts, paving tiles, truss lattices, drawn plank cracks). Some also mix a mini-scene with a flat graphic backdrop or fade the field to pastel. Real cards keep the background to a few large, quiet shapes and crop close.
